Consult Summary:
- Patient presents with a sudden-onset, severe headache for 3 days, partially responsive to ibuprofen and associated with photophobia and intermittent visual "shooting light" phenomena.
- Plan: in-person neurological examination including fundoscopy and blood pressure check; prescription of a stronger analgesic (details not documented); advice to attend emergency department if symptoms worsen.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Acute severe headache, possible migraine
- Presentation: sudden onset 3 days ago after waking; ongoing, largely continuous; pain described as global but worse over the right eye; severity reported as 8/10 falling to ~5/10 with analgesia.
- Associated symptoms: photophobia, intermittent “shooting light” visual phenomena, feeling a bit sick but no vomiting, occasional stabbing pain with quick standing or vigorous head movement.
- Pertinent negatives: no focal weakness, no numbness/tingling, no fever reported, no cough, no sinus symptoms, no epistaxis, no recent travel.
- Response to treatment: partially improved by ibuprofen (does not fully resolve).
- Relevant history: recent eye check reported as normal; family history: mother with severe migraines including vomiting.
- Provider assessment: possible migraine-type headache.
- Plan related to this issue: book face-to-face appointment for full neurological examination and fundoscopy; check blood pressure at that visit; prescribe a stronger analgesic to replace ibuprofen (medication name/dose/route/frequency not documented); advised can take paracetamol with the prescribed medication; take prescribed medication with food; if headache worsens markedly or changes, attend A&E.

Issue 2: Combined oral contraceptive use and headache safety
- Current use: patient takes "the pill" started about 1 year ago (brand/name not documented).
- Relevant history: blood pressure checked at pharmacy when starting the pill ~1 year ago and reported as normal.
- Clinical considerations: clinician advised that if patient has regular migraines with visual aura, the current pill may be unsuitable and may need to be changed.
- Plan related to this issue: blood pressure will be measured during the in-person examination to reassess pill appropriateness; continue current pill for the moment.

Issue 3: Functional impact / work impairment and decreased energy
- Work: works from home; has missed one full day and reduced work capacity on other days over the 3-day headache period.
- Symptoms affecting function: difficulty concentrating and completing work tasks; reports some lack of energy, attributed to headaches.
- Plan: address underlying headache; follow-up after face-to-face assessment; seek urgent care if symptoms worsen.

Medications:
- Combined oral contraceptive pill — brand/name not documented; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Ibuprofen — taken intermittently for headache; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Proposed stronger analgesic (prescription discussed) — name/dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Paracetamol — advised may be taken concurrently with prescribed analgesic; dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
- None reported.

Past Medical History:
- Remote unspecified pain when younger, no cause found, resolved (patient report).
- No other chronic medical problems reported.

Social History:
- Lives alone.
- Smoking: denies smoking.
- Alcohol: drinks alcohol approximately three (units/drinks) once weekly (patient estimate).

Preventative History:
- Recent eye check reported; no change in vision.
- Blood pressure checked at pharmacy ~1 year ago when starting the pill; reported as normal.
- No other preventative care measures (cervical screening, mammogram, PSA, FOBT, BMD, vaccinations, skin check, optometry visit dates) documented.

Physical Examination:
- No physical examination performed during this consultation.
- No vital signs documented.

Plan:
- Book an in-person appointment with support team for full neurological examination and fundoscopy.
- Measure blood pressure at the face-to-face visit to reassess contraceptive appropriateness.
- Prescribe a stronger analgesic to use instead of ibuprofen (medication name/dose/route/frequency to be documented on prescription).
- Patient advised to take prescribed medication with food and may take paracetamol concurrently.
- If symptoms settle before the appointment, the appointment can be cancelled.
- If headache worsens, becomes unbearable, or neurological signs develop, patient advised to attend A&E and/or contact clinic for urgent advice.
- Follow-up after face-to-face assessment as arranged by support team.
